- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in upward moves.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +3% above recent mean), apply a 1–3 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is trending up, cap the 30d forecast at +2% above recent 14d average to avoid overestimation.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 3+ points from recent peak), adjust forecast downward by 1–3 points for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.5–0.8) followed by a drop, reduce forecast slope to avoid momentum bias.
- For 30d forecasts, if the first 5 days show strong upward movement, apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to dampen early volatility.
